checks.evidence: Customer email footer 'Policy number: VER-1004'; Policy Schedule policy_id VER-1004, holder Thomas Petit; repair_quote.pdf header 'Insurer: Veridia Insurance, policy VER-1004'.

checks.sources_say: C2 (Collision damage) is in the Policy Schedule and fits a collision damaging the insured vehicle
checks.evidence: Policy Schedule coverages include code C2 'Collision damage'; contract Article 2 table: C2 covers 'Damage to the insured vehicle after a collision'; email describes hitting a post in a car park, damaging his own car.
Customer email: 'I hit a post in an underground car park on 27 October 2026.'
Email header 'Customer email received on 2026-10-28'; quote issued 28/10/2026, consistent.

repair_quote.pdf (quote Q-2610-5283): 'TOTAL INCL. VAT 1 640,00 €'; contract Article 1 defines repair cost as the total including VAT on the quote. The ~€900 in the email was only a phone estimate; the written quote is the source document.

checks.sources_say: Policyholder at fault (single-vehicle collision with a fixed object)
checks.evidence: Email: 'I hit a post... Nobody else was involved' — no other driver, so the authorised driver is at fault; the not-at-fault waiver (Article 5.2) therefore does not apply.
Email: 'Nobody else was involved.' Contract Article 1 defines third party as any person other than the authorised driver; a post is not a person.
Email states nobody else was involved, so there is no third party; consistent with third_party_involved=false and with Article 5.2 waiver being inapplicable.

checks.sources_say: C2 requires photos of the damage and the repair quote; both received and both belong to this policyholder/vehicle
checks.evidence: Contract Article 4.3 table: C2 requires 'Photos of the damage; repair quote' (accident report signed by both drivers only 'when a third party is involved' — none here). repair_quote.pdf is made out to Thomas Petit, policy VER-1004, Volkswagen Golf (2020), reg. FD-371-WS; damage_photos.zip is listed as an attachment of the email and, being mailroom-stored, counts as received per the review instructions.

Contract Article 3 exclusions (alcohol/drugs, invalid licence, racing, intentional damage, wear/mechanical failure only): the email and quote describe a single-vehicle collision with a post — none of the exclusion facts is stated anywhere, so no exclusion signal is correct.

verdict.summary: All recorded facts match the email, the repair quote and the Veridia contract, the claim was reported within 5 days under an in-schedule C2 coverage with the required documents and no exclusion or playbook referral trigger, so the staged payment of €1,340 (assessor already booked) should be approved.
